channel.title: Deal Math
channel.description: Real estate investing calculators and Texas and Oklahoma investor guides

item.title: How Texas Property Tax Sales Work for Investors
item.description: Texas tax sales explained: who holds them, the first-Tuesday schedule, online auctions, minimum bids, struck-off resales and the 2-year or 180-day redemption period.

item.title: Texas Foreclosure Process: How Nonjudicial Sales Work
item.description: The Texas nonjudicial foreclosure process for investors: the 20-day notice to cure on homesteads, 21-day notice of sale, first-Tuesday courthouse auctions and what buyers should check.

item.title: Buying Probate Property in Texas: What Investors Need to Know
item.description: How inherited property is transferred in Texas and what that means for buyers: the 4-year will deadline, muniment of title, small estate affidavits and affidavits of heirship.

item.title: Texas Sheriff and Constable Sales: How They Work
item.description: Texas sheriff and constable sales explained: what gets sold (execution and tax foreclosure sales), the first-Tuesday schedule, online auctions and a pre-bid checklist.

item.title: How Oklahoma Tax Sales Work: The June County Resale
item.description: Oklahoma tax sales explained for investors: land delinquent 3 or more years goes to the county treasurer's resale on the second Monday of June, in person or online.

item.title: Oklahoma Foreclosure Process: Judicial and Power of Sale
item.description: Oklahoma foreclosure for investors: judicial foreclosure and sheriff's sale, the Power of Sale Act's 35-day cure notice, the homestead election, appraisal and 30-day sale notice.

item.title: Buying Probate Property in Oklahoma: What Investors Need to Know
item.description: How inherited real estate is transferred in Oklahoma and what buyers should check: summary administration up to $200,000, the $50,000 small estate affidavit and who can sign the deed.

item.title: Oklahoma Sheriff Sales: Appraisal, Minimum Bid and Confirmation
item.description: Oklahoma sheriff sales explained: court-ordered sales after foreclosure, appraisal by three disinterested people, the two-thirds minimum bid, 30-day published notice and court confirmation.

item.title: 30-year mortgage rate eases to 7.18%, third weekly decline
item.description: Freddie Mac's weekly survey put the average 30-year fixed rate at 7.18% on November 5, down from 7.24% a week earlier but up from 6.22% a year ago.

item.title: Oklahoma voters reject SQ 847, keeping the 3% and 5% property value caps
item.description: State Question 847, which would have cut Oklahoma's yearly cap on taxable value growth from 3% to 1.75% for homesteads and ag land and from 5% to 4% for other property, failed on November 3.

item.title: Fed holds its target range at 3.75% to 4%, with two votes for a hike
item.description: The Federal Open Market Committee left the federal funds target range at 3-3/4 to 4 percent on October 28; Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase.

item.title: Texas home sales fell 4.7% from a year earlier in August as inventory stayed high
item.description: The Texas Real Estate Research Center reported 28,740 closed sales in August, down 4.7% year over year, a $330,000 median price and 5.3 months of inventory.

item.title: U.S. housing starts fell 5.2% in September to a 1.22 million pace
item.description: Census Bureau data showed September housing starts at a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1,221,000, down 5.2% from August and 7.4% from a year earlier; permits were 1,400,000.

item.title: Existing-home sales rose 1.5% in September; median price $417,500
item.description: NAR reported existing-home sales at a 3.99 million annual rate in September, up 1.5% from August and down 2.2% from a year earlier, with a 4.8-month supply.
